data.name: Niket
data.gender_notes: Niket is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Niket is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Niketa' which means 'victory', 'triumph' or 'conqueror'. This name is often used in Hindu mythology for gods and warriors who have achieved great victories. The name Niket carries the meaning “Victory, Triumph” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Niket usually hope their child will grow to embody victory, triumph and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the triumph of the human spirit over adversity.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Niket total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Niket holds great cultural significance in Hindu society as it is associated with victorious gods and warriors. It is also used as a name for children, instilling in them a sense of strength, courage, and determination from a young age.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Niket lies in its connection to the divine. Niket is a reminder of the power of the universe and the potential for personal growth and self-realization. It encourages individuals to strive towards victory over their inner demons and to triumph in their spiritual journey. Additionally, it can serve as a reminder of the Hindu deity Niketaswa, who is believed to protect his devotees and grant them victory over their challenges.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Niket is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Niketana', meaning 'one who has reached, attained or resides in a sacred or peaceful place'. It symbolizes an individual who has found inner peace and spiritual growth, living in harmony with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Niketas of Arados, a 5th century Indian philosopher and teacher, was an important intermediary in the transmission of Hindu thought to the Greeks and the West. He was sent to Constantinople by the Gupta emperor Skandagupta to promote Buddhism and Hinduism and to seek diplomatic ties with the Byzantine Empire.
historical_references.context: Transmission of Hindu and Buddhist thought to the Greeks and the West

historical_references.reference: Niketas of Thessalonica, a 12th century Byzantine scholar and bishop, wrote extensively on Indian philosophy and religion. He translated several Hindu texts into Greek and is known for his commentary on the Bhagavad Gita.
historical_references.context: Transmission of Hindu texts and philosophy into Greek
